name: Keyboard Maestro
description: Keyboard Maestro is a Mac automation platform for building macros that control applications, websites, windows, text, images, files, clipboards, and system behavior. Its triggers and hundreds of actions let users combine UI control, scripting, conditions, loops, scheduling, and local data into simple shortcuts or complex workflows.
agentUseSummary: Keyboard Maestro cannot yet be connected to Relay agents because macros run through an installed Mac engine with broad local permissions and arbitrary-code authority, while its local web server and unauthenticated remote-trigger URLs do not provide a bounded, reliable, provider-authenticated cloud API contract.

blocked.label: Connect Keyboard Maestro
blocked.description: Relay does not present a license, installed engine, local macro library, macOS security permission, web-server login, or remote-trigger URL as a Railway API connection.

blocked.label: Control the local engine
blocked.description: Relay does not invoke kmtrigger URLs, the keyboardmaestro CLI, AppleScript, scripts, the built-in web server, local variables, clipboards, macros, or private application-support files.

blocked.label: Use remote macro triggers
blocked.description: Relay does not collect or call unauthenticated Remote trigger URLs, expose Public Web macros, store local web-server credentials, or treat URL secrecy and best-effort delivery as provider authentication and truthful execution status.

blocked.label: Execute Mac automation
blocked.description: UI control, keystrokes, clipboard access, screen capture, file and browser actions, communication, downloads, scripts, commands, application control, and other macro effects remain unavailable until Relay ships explicit local authority and bounded approvals.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until Relay ships a separately disclosed, user-authorized Mac-local connector with a pinned typed macro allowlist and no arbitrary-code or public-trigger surface.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay does not silently bridge OpenClaw to Keyboard Maestro's local engine, macro library, web server, remote triggers, scripts, permissions, or private data.
Relay does not silently bridge Hermes to Keyboard Maestro's local engine, macro library, web server, remote triggers, scripts, permissions, or private data.

providerSetup.blocker: Keyboard Maestro macros are stored and executed on the user's Mac and can automate nearly any manual Mac action, access persistent variables and clipboards, control applications and websites, and execute arbitrary shell, AppleScript, JavaScript, Swift, and Automator code. The app requires broad macOS security permissions including Accessibility and, for some actions, Screen Recording. Its built-in web server is disabled by default; authenticated login can execute every active macro, while Public Web triggers can be invoked without credentials. Stairways' Internet Remote trigger is also unauthenticated, identified only by URL values, explicitly unreliable, and documented as carrying serious security risk. None of these surfaces is a bounded provider-authenticated API with typed actions and truthful results, and Relay's current Marketplace runtime excludes local-app command execution.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request license details, web-server credentials, remote-trigger URLs, macOS permissions, macro files, variables, clipboards, or local state; enable servers or triggers; import macros; run scripts, CLI commands, AppleScript, or URLs; automate the app UI; or show Connect. Reconsider after Relay ships a disclosed Mac-local connector that verifies app and engine presence, obtains explicit permissions, exposes only reviewed typed macros by immutable identifier, validates inputs and outputs, blocks arbitrary code and public triggers, requires approval for external effects, redacts secrets, audits calls, and never falls back to the unauthenticated trigger service.

evidence.supports: Keyboard Maestro describes a Mac automation engine that controls applications, websites, text, images, files, windows, clipboards, and system behavior using hundreds of combinable actions.
Keyboard Maestro states that macros are stored locally in the user's Mac account and are not tied to the license or synchronized through a provider cloud.

Keyboard Maestro documents local URL, CLI, AppleScript, and scripting triggers, a separately enabled local web server, Remote triggers, local macro storage, and the risk of imported macros executing damaging behavior.

Keyboard Maestro documents broad macOS security authority and a disabled-by-default local web server where authenticated users can execute all active macros and Public Web triggers can execute without authentication.

Keyboard Maestro states that Internet Remote triggers have no authentication, can be invoked by anyone who knows or collides with the URL identifiers, are not guaranteed, and carry serious security risk.
Keyboard Maestro's official action reference documents execution of embedded or external shell scripts and command-line programs with access to selected macro variables and configurable outputs.
